title: Attachments and media
lede: What you can attach, where it goes, and the limits that will stop you.

blocks.text: Attachments work at two levels. An **assessment-level** attachment stays available for the whole exam, which suits a formulary, a lab reference sheet, or a case study. You set it on the Assessment Options page, students reach it any time through the **Exam Controls** menu in Examplify, and you get exactly one per assessment. A **question-level** attachment only opens while the student is on that question, and a question can carry several.

blocks.title: Only one file at assessment level
blocks.text: If your exam needs several shared references, combine them into one file first, usually a single PDF. Work that out before the draft deadline rather than during OME proofing.

blocks.title: 200 MB total per assessment
blocks.text: That ceiling covers every attachment and every inline image in the assessment added together, not each file separately. An image-heavy exam will reach it. If you are building one, budget for it early.

blocks.title: Where these numbers come from
blocks.text: The image, audio, and video limits appear in both the OME onboarding documents and the vendor article. The PDF and RTF limits come from the vendor article alone, since the OME documents never listed them. They should be accurate, but JABSOM has not exercised them.

items: Resize images to 1920 x 1080 or smaller before uploading. An oversized file gets rejected rather than resized for you.
Radiology and histology images are usually what pushes an exam toward the 200 MB ceiling. Compress rather than crop when diagnostic detail matters.
Video plays on the device in a secure exam. Test it on an iPad during OME preview, because desktop playback tells you very little.
